_about: Intended outcome for every scenario in demo/scenarios. 'alerts' is the DETECTION outcome (deterministic statistics, asserted exactly by internal/pipeline/scenarios_test.go - no model involved). 'intended_severity' is the band a good diagnosis should land in (checked for Bedrock by `go run ./compare -bedrock`). 'mock_action' is what the offline mock explainer + the dispatch table produce, asserted by the tests. Sensor faults never reach a model: their action comes straight from the dispatch table.

01-etch12-normal.why: Baseline: every sensor at its usual level and noise. False-positive check.

02-cvd04-normal.why: Baseline on a different tool type.

03-imp02-normal.why: Baseline on a third tool type.

04-etch12-pressure-gradual-drift.why: Slow creep: no single reading is alarming and it never crosses the spec-sheet limit. Caught because the EWMA baseline moves 4 sigma away from the warm-up reference.

05-cvd04-particle-spike.why: One reading at ~15 sigma: the spike rule fires immediately.

06-cmp07-noisy-within-bounds.why: Three times the usual noise but no trend or shift. The detector learns this tool's own noise; a fixed spec limit false-alarms here (see compare/).

07-imp02-vacuum-gauge-stuck.why: The value looks normal but never changes: a real analog gauge always wiggles. Sensor fault -> ticket, no model call.

08-etch12-temp-dropout.why: Three missing readings in a row. Missing data is neither zero nor normal. Sensor fault -> ticket, no model call.

09-cvd04-threshold-boundary.why: heater_temp reads z = 3.000 three times (ON the >= 3.0 cutoff: flags). rf_power reads 3.000 only twice then 2.997 three times: never flags. The evidence is weak, so the explanation is low-confidence and the dispatch table sends it to a human rather than dismissing it.

10-cmp07-correlated-drift.why: Three sensors on one tool drift together. Grouped into ONE alert (one diagnosis per incident, not three pages); the explanation must reason about the correlation.
